subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for every legacy ownerless row, accepting that existing plugin workflows may require operator recovery after upgrade?
rationale: Ownership cannot be inferred safely for legacy rows, but unconditional rejection changes existing upgrade behavior and therefore needs explicit security and compatibility ownership.

options.title: Fail closed with recovery guidance
options.body: Keep ownerless rows inaccessible to plugin runtimes, document the operator recovery path, and prove fresh and upgraded behavior before merge.

options.title: Add a trusted migration
options.body: Delay enforcement until a narrowly defined migration can assign ownership only where durable provenance proves the correct plugin.

options.title: Preserve legacy ownerless access
options.body: Allow plugin-runtime patches on ownerless rows for compatibility, accepting that this leaves an ambiguous cross-plugin authorization boundary.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with recovery guidance
recommendation.body: Keep ownerless rows inaccessible to plugin runtimes, document the operator recovery path, and prove fresh and upgraded behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway security and authorization history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the compatibility-versus-isolation decision.
